_note: The parameter catalogue for this corpus: every number a statute did not state, with its unit (the corpus's own units are accepted and scaled by the decoder), the convention its value comes from and its source. It starts empty: the plan decides which parameters exist and proposes each with a provisional value, and the harness enters the proposal here marked `proposed` (run, iteration, node) until the operator reviews it by removing the marker or changing the value; the doctor lists every unreviewed proposal. The operator-authored list this file carried before any law was planned is kept, out of the pipeline's path, under readings/legacy/. Figures the law states are literals on the rule's span, never entries here.

params.name: p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph
params.convention: The sampling period of the carla_scene_graph acquisition standard, 20 Hz (one scene every 50 ms): the step bound of headingSince, the largest gap between two consecutive scenes it integrates across; not a look-back window and not an action window.

params.name: p.standstill_speed_tolerance
params.convention: Standstill convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed reading is read as the definition's complete cessation from movement, set at the noise floor of vehicle speed measurement so that a standing vehicle is not reported as moving and a creeping one is not reported as halted.
params.source: stop-detection thresholds used in naturalistic-driving and vehicle-dynamics data reduction

params.name: p.stop_point_tolerance
params.convention: Stop-point convention of the approach reading: the bound within which a halt counts as at the place the words name (the crossing, the stop line, the view point), covering the lateral and longitudinal error of the map's mark and of the body outline.
params.source: stop-line compliance field studies and lane-level map accuracy specifications

params.name: p.intersecting_way_view_distance
params.convention: Intersection sight-distance convention: the length of the intersecting way that must be visible in each direction from the stopping point for a driver to judge a gap and clear the junction, taken from the departure sight triangle for a minor-road stop at a major road of ordinary speed.
params.source: AASHTO Green Book, intersection sight distance (case B)

params.name: p.reverse_speed_tolerance
params.convention: Rearward-motion convention: the magnitude of the velocity component along the body's heading below which a rearward reading is indistinguishable from measurement noise in a standing vehicle, set at the noise floor of vehicle speed measurement.
params.source: stop-detection and direction-of-travel thresholds in vehicle-dynamics data reduction

params.name: p.turn_recognition_window
params.convention: Manoeuvre-recognition convention: the window behind an observation over which a yaw rate is integrated to tell a bending path from straight running at a junction, taken from the duration of a low-speed corner manoeuvre.
params.source: manoeuvre-segmentation windows used in naturalistic-driving analyses

params.name: p.heading_change_noise_floor
params.convention: Resolution convention: the heading change over the recognition window below which an integrated yaw reading is indistinguishable from straight running at the acquisition profile's sampling rate; it names the source's resolution only and no size of turn.
params.source: yaw-rate sensor and scene-graph heading resolution figures

params.name: p.same_direction_cosine_tolerance
params.convention: Heading-agreement convention: the cosine of the largest angle between two headings still read as the same direction, set at thirty degrees so that a vehicle in a bend or beginning a lane change is still read as travelling with the stream.
params.source: heading-tolerance values used in lane-level trajectory conflict analyses

params.name: p.following_headway_time_dry
params.convention: Time-headway convention on a dry surface: the headway that multiplies the follower's speed to give the gap within which a leader's deceleration cannot be answered, the two-second rule.
params.source: two-second-rule driver guidance and AASHTO perception-reaction time

params.name: p.following_headway_time_wet
params.convention: Time-headway convention on a wet surface: the dry headway increased for the longer braking distance of a wet pavement.
params.source: wet-pavement friction factors in AASHTO stopping-sight-distance models

params.name: p.following_headway_time_ice
params.convention: Time-headway convention on ice or snow: the dry headway increased for the much longer braking distance of an icy or snow-covered pavement.
params.source: winter-surface friction factors in highway design practice

params.name: p.following_headway_time_adverse_geometry
params.convention: Time-headway convention on a steep or curved stretch: the dry headway increased where a downgrade lengthens braking distance or a bend shortens the view of the vehicle ahead.
params.source: AASHTO grade and horizontal-curve corrections to stopping sight distance

params.name: p.following_reaction_time
params.convention: Perception-reaction convention: the time over which a closing speed is carried before the follower's brakes act, which turns the excess of the follower's speed over the leader's into an added gap requirement.
params.source: AASHTO Green Book perception-reaction time

params.name: p.following_grade_threshold
params.convention: Grade convention: the magnitude of longitudinal slope above which the design correction to braking distance becomes material, so that the headway bound moves to the adverse-geometry selection.
params.source: AASHTO grade corrections to stopping sight distance

params.name: p.following_curvature_threshold
params.convention: Curvature convention: the horizontal curvature above which a bend materially shortens the view of the vehicle ahead on an ordinary highway, a radius of about one hundred metres.
params.source: AASHTO horizontal-curve design radii

params.name: p.following_dense_traffic_count
params.convention: Traffic-density convention: the number of road users of the traffic aggregate on the subject's highway at which the stream is read as dense enough to call for the added gap.
params.source: level-of-service density bands in highway capacity practice

params.name: p.following_dense_traffic_gap_increment
params.convention: Traffic-density convention: the gap added to the headway bound in dense traffic, covering the shorter warning a follower has when vehicles ahead of the leader may brake.
params.source: car-following model jam-spacing figures

params.name: p.overtaking_min_speed_excess
params.convention: Passing convention: the excess of the overtaking road user's speed over the overtaken one's below which the two are keeping station rather than passing, set at the resolution of a speed difference.
params.source: overtaking-manoeuvre identification thresholds in trajectory data studies

params.name: p.conditions_permit_min_speed
params.convention: Traffic-flow feasibility convention: the speed below which running is queued or stop-and-go, so that holding a long space ahead is not possible, taken from the boundary between congested and free-flow operation.
params.source: speed-flow curves and congested-regime boundaries in highway capacity practice

params.name: p.conditions_permit_max_intervening_users
params.convention: Traffic-flow feasibility convention: the number of other vehicles that may occupy the space ahead before the subject is read as unable to hold it, since a vehicle that moves into the space closes it without any act of the subject.
params.source: gap-closure observations in heavy-vehicle platooning field trials

params.name: p.caravan_min_members
params.convention: Procession convention: the number of road users travelling one behind another at which the group is read as a file rather than as two vehicles happening to follow one another, taken from the smallest group that presents a continuous obstacle to an entering vehicle.
params.source: convoy and platoon definitions in traffic-operations practice

params.name: p.caravan_max_member_gap
params.convention: Procession convention: the reach within which another road user is read as travelling with the subject in the same file, beyond which the two are independent vehicles on the same highway.
params.source: platoon-identification headway and spacing thresholds in traffic-flow studies

params.name: p.entry_vehicle_length
params.convention: Gap-acceptance convention: the length of the design vehicle that must fit into the space, used where no entering road user is in the scene whose own read length could be used instead.
params.source: design-vehicle dimensions for a passenger car in highway geometric design

params.name: p.entry_clearance_headway_time
params.convention: Gap-acceptance convention: the clear headway in front of and behind an entering vehicle, at the speed of the stream, below which the entry is not a safe one; the critical gap is the vehicle's length plus twice this headway.
params.source: critical-gap values for lane-change and merging manoeuvres in capacity analysis

params.name: p.wrong_way_speed_tolerance
params.convention: Direction-of-travel convention: the magnitude of the velocity component along a designated direction below which travel against that direction is not distinguished from standing, from lateral drift, or from the error of the mapped direction and the measured velocity.
params.source: wrong-way-driving detection thresholds in traffic-surveillance practice

params.name: p.turn_signal_advance_window
params.convention: Signalling convention: the window behind the movement within which an indication counts as the signal given for it, taken from the advance warning a lane change is expected to carry; it is a stated recognition bound for the look-back and not a requirement of duration.
params.source: turn-signal advance-warning intervals in driver guidance and signalling-compliance studies

params.name: p.lane_change_entry_headway_time
params.convention: Gap-acceptance convention: the headway, at the speed of the faster of the two road users, that the longitudinal clearance to a road user in the lane entered must cover for the entry to be an accepted gap.
params.source: critical-gap values for lane-change manoeuvres in capacity analysis

params.name: p.lane_change_min_clearance
params.convention: Conflict-avoidance convention: the clearance between bodies below which an approach is read as a conflict rather than a safe passing distance, used both as the floor of the entry clearance and as the bound on the closest approach.
params.source: surrogate-safety-measure clearance thresholds in conflict analysis

params.name: p.lane_change_conflict_horizon
params.convention: Conflict-avoidance convention: the time ahead of the observation over which a closest approach under constant velocities is tested, taken from the horizon used for surrogate conflict measures.
params.source: time-to-collision horizons in surrogate-safety-measure practice

params.name: p.lateral_offset_resolution
params.convention: Lateral-offset convention: the magnitude of a signed lateral offset below which the side a region lies on is not distinguished from straddling it, covering the error of the mapped boundary and the measured heading and position.
params.source: lane-level map accuracy and positioning-error specifications

params.name: p.turn_onset_yaw_rate
params.convention: Manoeuvre-onset convention: the rate of change of heading above which a body is read as turning rather than running straight with sensor noise and small corrections, which fixes the observed beginning from which a turn's heading change is counted.
params.source: yaw-rate onset thresholds in manoeuvre-segmentation practice

params.name: p.left_turn_angle
params.convention: Turn-recognition convention: the heading change accumulated since the onset at which a turn to the left is recognized as a turn rather than a lane change or a curve, taken from the smallest angle a junction turn subtends.
params.source: turn-classification angle thresholds in trajectory-based manoeuvre recognition

params.name: p.u_turn_reversal_angle
params.convention: Reversal convention: the accumulated heading change at which the definition's proceeding in the opposite direction is recognized, set below a half turn so that a reversal completed between sampled observations or on a skewed way is still recognized.
params.source: U-turn detection angle thresholds in trajectory-based manoeuvre recognition

params.name: p.cautious_proceed_max_speed
params.convention: Low-speed stopping-distance convention: the speed at or below which a vehicle moving off from a required halt into a junction can be brought to rest within the junction's conflict area on seeing a road user it must give way to, taken as the 10 mph figure design practice uses for a stop-controlled entry.
params.source: AASHTO Green Book stopping-sight-distance table at low design speeds, and the MUTCD practice of treating a stop-controlled entry as a crawl speed.

params.name: p.yield_conflict_horizon
params.convention: Conflict-avoidance convention: the time ahead of the observation over which a closest approach under constant velocities is read as the 'danger of a crash' the right-of-way definition names, rather than as a passing of two road users on diverging paths.
params.source: Surrogate-safety practice for time-to-conflict measures at junctions (post-encroachment and time-to-collision thresholds of two to three seconds).

params.name: p.yield_min_clearance
params.convention: Conflict-avoidance convention: the clearance between the nearest points of two bodies below which a closest approach is read as a failure to grant precedence rather than as a safe passing.
params.source: Lateral and longitudinal clearance practice for passing a road user at low speed in a junction.

params.name: p.simultaneous_entry_window
params.convention: Arrival-simultaneity convention: the interval between two vehicles' entries into one junction within which the two are still both inside the junction's conflict area at ordinary approach speeds, so that their entries count as at approximately the same time; taken as the time a vehicle needs to clear the conflict area of a small urban junction at a crossing speed.
params.source: Gap-acceptance and conflict-area clearance practice for unsignalised junctions (critical gap and follow-up headway tables of the Highway Capacity Manual).

params.name: p.yield_headway_time
params.convention: Gap-acceptance convention: the headway, at the approaching vehicle's own speed, within which that vehicle is read as so close to the junction as to constitute an immediate hazard, being the time a turning or crossing vehicle needs to clear its path.
params.source: Critical gap and follow-up headway practice for permitted left turns and crossing manoeuvres (Highway Capacity Manual).

params.name: p.yield_sign_slowed_max_speed
params.convention: Yield-sign approach convention: the speed at or below which a vehicle at a yield-controlled entrance counts as having slowed, so that it can give way at the entrance without a mandatory halt; taken as the crawl speed design practice assigns to a yield-controlled approach.
params.source: AASHTO Green Book and MUTCD practice for yield-controlled approaches, where a 10 mph approach speed is the design basis for giving way without stopping.

params.name: p.centerline_adjacent_distance
params.convention: Lane-position convention: the lateral distance from the centre line within which a place on the right half of a two-directional highway counts as the portion nearest the centre line, set at one design lane width, the width of a single line of vehicles beside the centre line.
params.source: AASHTO Green Book design lane widths for urban arterials (3.0 to 3.6 m).

params.name: p.curvature_resolution
params.convention: Map-geometry resolution convention: the magnitude of horizontal curvature below which a surveyed road alignment is indistinguishable from a tangent at the resolution of the source, a radius of the order of a kilometre. It names the source's resolution only and sets no bound on how sharp a bend must be for the duty to bind.
params.source: highway alignment survey practice, in which curves of radius above about a kilometre are recorded as tangents in the road geometry of a map or simulator.

params.name: p.crest_approach_distance
params.convention: Crest sight-distance convention: the distance from a crest within which the crest's vertical curve restricts the view of the road beyond it, taken as the length of the crest vertical curve of the design standard at open-road design speed; it bounds 'the approach to or near' the crest on either side.
params.source: AASHTO Green Book crest vertical curve lengths and stopping sight distance tables for open-road design speeds.

params.name: p.reasonable_speed_base_limit
params.convention: Design-speed convention: the speed a dry, wide, level, straight and unobstructed open-road stretch supports, before any correction for surface, stream, slope or sight; it is the upper anchor of the reasonable-speed bound and is lowered by every factor the standard names.
params.source: AASHTO Green Book design-speed table for rural arterial highways (the 65 mph design speed).

params.name: p.reasonable_speed_wet_decrement
params.convention: Wet-pavement convention: the reduction from the dry design speed that keeps the braking distance of the stopping-distance model unchanged on a wet surface, about a tenth of the design speed.
params.source: AASHTO Green Book wet-pavement friction factors used in the stopping-sight-distance model.

params.name: p.reasonable_speed_ice_decrement
params.convention: Winter-surface convention: the larger reduction from the dry design speed that keeps the braking distance unchanged on an icy or snow-covered surface, whose friction is a small fraction of the dry value.
params.source: winter maintenance practice and the low-friction end of the AASHTO braking-distance model.

params.name: p.reasonable_speed_traffic_decrement_per_user
params.convention: Traffic-density convention: the reduction of the bound for each road user of the scene present on the highway the subject occupies, so that the bound falls as the stream thickens and the space to react shortens.
params.source: the speed-flow relations of the Highway Capacity Manual, whose free-flow speed falls steadily as flow on a segment rises.

params.name: p.reasonable_speed_grade_decrement_per_unit_grade
params.convention: Grade-correction convention: the reduction of the bound per unit of longitudinal slope magnitude, taken from the grade correction of the braking-distance model, so that a few per cent of slope costs a little over a metre per second.
params.source: AASHTO Green Book stopping-sight-distance tables with grade corrections for downgrades.

params.name: p.reasonable_speed_lane_width_time
params.convention: Lateral-recovery convention: the time within which a driver must correct a lateral excursion of the order of the lane's width; dividing the lane width by it turns the width into a speed bound, so that a narrower lane bounds the speed in proportion to its width and a standard lane yields a bound near the open-road design speed.
params.source: lane-keeping and lateral-recovery times of vehicle-dynamics practice, calibrated against the standard 3.6 m lane and the design speed.

params.name: p.reasonable_speed_sight_time
params.convention: Stopping-sight-distance convention: the perception-reaction plus braking time over which the available sight must cover the distance the vehicle travels; dividing the place's sight distance, or the visibility distance, by it gives the speed at which the vehicle can still stop within what can be seen.
params.source: AASHTO Green Book brake-reaction time of 2.5 s used in the stopping-sight-distance model.

declarations.meaning: the map or trace declares that the highway the road user occupies at the observation lies inside the territorial limits of a city
the map or trace declares that the stretch of highway the road user occupies at the observation lies outside a business district
the source's current plan for the road user is that it turn to the left at the region named as the declaration's target
the source's current plan for the road user is that it turn, to either hand, at the region named as the declaration's target
the map or trace declares that the stretch of highway the road user occupies at the observation lies within a business district or a residential district

_fields.aggregates: optional operator overrides only: word, classes (ru.* ids or other words). The run derives every aggregate the laws use from the corpus definitions (results/<run>/reading.json, for review); an operator entry here takes precedence over the derived one.
